newsitem.title: INDIA: Rebounding Indian stocks may stop for breather.
newsitem.headline: Rebounding Indian stocks may stop for breather.

text.p: Scattered profit-taking is expected to halt rebounding Indian stock markets in the holiday-shortened week because traders would not want to keep open positions during the Christmas vacation, analysts said.
"We expect the markets to retract some gains made over the last three weeks," said Sanjay D'Souza, senior manager at investment firm Nucleus Securities Ltd.

"The bear covering is mostly over and we feel the bull operators will not want to keep their positions open, especially since the political situation continues to remain fluid," he said in a note at the weekend.

The top-30 stock index of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) surged 228.54 points, or 7.93 percent, to 3,110.19 last week. The index has recovered 14.63 percent since December 4 when it hit a three-year low of 2,713.12.

Traders said the latest rise was bolstered by political developments which they believe could lead to the revival of the Congress, India's decades-old ruling party until it was defeated in May elections.
The hope was sparked by the resignation on Thursday of former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao from his last party post as the head of its group in parliament.
Rao is battling three corruption cases and a growing number of critics. He has denied any wrongdoing in the cases.
Political instability fears caused unease in the markets and traders blamed the 13-party United Front (UF) government for an economic slowdown and shrinking company profits.
Equity analysts said former finance minister Manmohan Singh, the architect of India's economic reforms, is a likely choice as the Congress's parliamentary party chief.
"We feel that Mr Manmohan Singh would emerge as a strong contender for the post given his unsullied image and general acceptability within the party," D'Souza said.
"With a stronger Congress the UF government would be forced to be on its toes. We expect the next budget to be much more people, industry and market-friendly," he said.
One broker said the market undercurrent was better and this could drive prices up in the last two days of trade in 1996.
"The mood is one of expectancy," said Bharat Dhanki at brokerage Vrajlal G. Dhanki. "I see a much more robust closing." He expects the BSE index to finish at 3,170.
D'Souza projected the index to move between 2,975 and 3,150 this week.
The BSE and most other bourses are open only on Monday and Tuesday before they close for the holidays. The BSE re-opens on January 1, but the National Stock Exchange will resume on December 30.
